title: Logitech G502 LIGHTSPEED: Is the Wireless G502 Still Worth Buying?
summary: The G502 LIGHTSPEED is the wireless version of Logitech's best-known gaming mouse: HERO 25K sensor, 11 programmable buttons, tunable weights and POWERPLAY wireless charging. With micro-USB charging, a 114 g body and the newer G502 X PLUS on shelves, is it still a good buy?
description:
## Who is it for?

- Right-handed palm grippers with medium to large hands.
- MMO and MOBA players who want lots of buttons for macros.
- Anyone who already owns a POWERPLAY charging mat.

## Why consider it?

- Logitech lists a HERO 25K sensor (100–25,600 DPI) and a 1,000 Hz report rate over LIGHTSPEED wireless.
- 11 programmable buttons and a scroll wheel that switches between free-spin and notched modes.
- Tunable weights and POWERPLAY wireless charging support.

sections.title: What is the Logitech G502 LIGHTSPEED?
sections.content:
The G502 is one of Logitech's best-known gaming mice, famous for its sculpted right-handed shape, lots of buttons and adjustable weights. The G502 LIGHTSPEED, launched in 2019, was the first wireless version. It keeps the shape and 11-button layout of the wired G502 HERO and adds the HERO 25K sensor and LIGHTSPEED 2.4 GHz wireless.

Logitech lists it at 114 g (mouse only). PCWorld noted that this made it the lightest G502 at launch, below the wired G502 HERO's 121 g, thanks to an internal endoskeleton and 1.2 mm shell walls. Logitech's US store lists it at US$119.99, and it is frequently discounted now that the G502 X family has taken over the top of the range.

sections.title: Shape, weight and tunable weights
sections.content:
At 131.2 × 75.2 × 40 mm, it's a large, right-handed ergonomic mouse with a thumb rest on the left side. PCWorld found the shape unchanged from earlier G502s and called it one of the most comfortable mice its reviewer had used. It suits a palm grip and medium to large hands best.

The box includes six weights — four 2 g and two 4 g — for up to 16 g extra, so the mouse can range from about 114 g to 130 g. The 2 g weights go in a side tray; the 4 g weights sit in the round bay underneath. That bay is also where the POWERPLAY module goes, so if you charge on a POWERPLAY mat you lose the 4 g weight slots (PCWorld). If you're used to 60 g FPS mice, 114 g will feel heavy; if you like a planted, weighty mouse, that's a plus.

sections.title: HERO 25K sensor, buttons and scroll wheel
sections.content:
Logitech lists the HERO 25K sensor at 100–25,600 DPI, 400+ IPS and a 1,000 Hz report rate. Tracking accuracy is not something you need to worry about here. What it does **not** offer is the 4,000–8,000 Hz polling some newer esports mice support.

The 11 programmable buttons include the two main buttons with metal-spring tensioning, two buttons beside the left click, a thumb button cluster, a wheel-mode toggle and left/right wheel tilt. The wheel switches between free-spin for long pages and notched scrolling. PCWorld felt the LIGHTSPEED's lighter, rubber-coated wheel is less substantial than the solid metal wheel on earlier G502s. Onboard memory means saved DPI and button settings work on computers without G HUB installed.

sections.title: Battery, micro-USB charging and POWERPLAY
sections.content:
Logitech rates the battery at up to 60 hours with lighting off and up to 48 hours with default lighting — roughly one to two weeks of a few hours' play per day. RGB is limited to the G logo and DPI indicator, so turning it off to save battery costs little.

The weak point today is the micro-USB charging port. Buyer reviews on Best Buy mention that the port is recessed and only some micro-USB cables fit, so keep the included cable. The fix is a POWERPLAY wireless charging mat (sold separately and not cheap), which charges the mouse while it sits on the pad. If you'd rather have USB-C, look at the G502 X PLUS instead.

sections.title: G502 versions compared — and how it stacks up against the G102 / G203
sections.content:
The G502 name covers several models, so check the exact one before you buy:

- **G502 HERO** (wired): same shape and 11 buttons, 121 g, much cheaper — the pick if you don't need wireless.
- **G502 LIGHTSPEED** (this review): wireless, 114 g, micro-USB charging, POWERPLAY support.
- **G502 X / G502 X LIGHTSPEED / G502 X PLUS**: the redesigned generation with LIGHTFORCE switches; the wireless models charge over USB-C and the PLUS adds an RGB strip. More expensive.

Compared with the **Logitech G102 / G203 LIGHTSYNC** we've also covered, the G203 is a wired, symmetrical, 6-button mouse at about 85 g for a fraction of the price. It's the better basic gaming mouse on a budget; the G502 LIGHTSPEED is for people who want wireless, lots of buttons and a right-handed shape. If you want an ultralight wireless FPS mouse, the VXE R1 SE (about 51–55 g) is a completely different approach.

sections.title: Who should buy it — and who shouldn't
sections.content:
**Buy it if you:**
- Use a palm grip with medium to large right hands.
- Play MMOs, MOBAs or anything that benefits from extra buttons, or use macros for work.
- Already own (or plan to buy) a POWERPLAY mat and never want to think about charging.
- Can find it at a good discount and like a heavier mouse.

**Skip it if you:**
- Play competitive FPS and prefer mice under 70 g.
- Want USB-C charging or need Bluetooth for a tablet or a laptop with few ports.
- Are left-handed or use a claw or fingertip grip with small hands.
- Just need a basic mouse — the G203 or the wired G502 HERO cost far less.

sections.title: Sources for this review
sections.content: Zero Technology has not used this mouse in person. This is a research roundup based on Logitech's official product and technical specification pages (dimensions, weight, sensor, battery, box contents), PCWorld's review (shape, scroll wheel, weights and POWERPLAY), Best Buy buyer reviews and LanOC's review (micro-USB port and cable), and Logitech's US store listing for price, all checked in November 2026. See the Sources list at the end of this review. Images are official Logitech G product photos.

sections.title: Should you buy the Logitech G502 LIGHTSPEED?
sections.content: The G502 LIGHTSPEED is still an excellent wireless mouse for sensor quality, comfort and button count — everything that made the G502 famous. In 2026, though, micro-USB charging, a 114 g body and the existence of the G502 X PLUS mean it's really only worth buying **at a solid discount** or if you already own a POWERPLAY mat. If it costs close to the G502 X PLUS, get the newer mouse; if you don't need wireless, the wired G502 HERO gives you the same shape for much less.

pros: 11 programmable buttons and a dual-mode scroll wheel — great for MMOs, MOBAs and productivity shortcuts.
Logitech's HERO 25K sensor (100–25,600 DPI) is accurate enough for any genre.
Low-latency LIGHTSPEED 2.4 GHz wireless at a 1,000 Hz report rate.
Tunable 2 g and 4 g weights let you adjust weight and balance.
POWERPLAY compatible: charge on the mat while you play and forget about the battery.
Onboard memory keeps DPI and button settings on computers without G HUB.
cons: 114 g before weights — much heavier than 50–60 g ultralight FPS mice such as the VXE R1 SE.
Charges over dated micro-USB, and buyers report the recessed port doesn't fit every cable.
No Bluetooth: 2.4 GHz receiver or cable only.
Using POWERPLAY takes the slot for the 4 g weights, limiting weight tuning (PCWorld).
Right-handed only; the large, long shape doesn't suit small hands with a claw or fingertip grip.
Replaced at the top of the range by the G502 X PLUS, which charges over USB-C.
buying_advice: Worth buying for right-handed palm grippers who want lots of buttons or already own a POWERPLAY mat — ideally at a discount. If it costs close to the G502 X PLUS, buy the newer model.

faq.question: What's the difference between the G502 LIGHTSPEED and the G502 HERO?
faq.answer: Same shape, same 11 buttons and the same HERO 25K sensor. The LIGHTSPEED is wireless (rechargeable battery, POWERPLAY support) and lighter at 114 g versus 121 g; the HERO is wired and much cheaper.

faq.question: Does the G502 LIGHTSPEED have Bluetooth?
faq.answer: No. It connects only through the LIGHTSPEED 2.4 GHz USB receiver, or by cable while charging.

faq.question: How does the G502 LIGHTSPEED charge, and how long does the battery last?
faq.answer: With the included micro-USB cable, or wirelessly on a POWERPLAY mat (sold separately). Logitech rates the battery at up to 60 hours with lighting off and 48 hours with default lighting.

faq.question: Should I buy the G502 LIGHTSPEED or the G502 X PLUS?
faq.answer: The G502 X PLUS is the successor: redesigned, USB-C charging, LIGHTFORCE switches and more RGB. If the price gap is small, get the X PLUS; the LIGHTSPEED only makes sense at a good discount.

faq.question: Is the G502 LIGHTSPEED good for FPS games like Valorant and CS2?
faq.answer: The sensor is more than accurate enough, but at 114 g it's much heavier than modern FPS mice. If FPS is your main genre and you flick a lot, a lighter mouse such as the VXE R1 SE or the Logitech G203 (about 85 g) will suit you better.

faq.question: How does it compare with the Logitech G102 / G203?
faq.answer: The G502 LIGHTSPEED is wireless, has 11 buttons (the G203 has 6), a higher-end HERO 25K sensor, tunable weights and a right-handed shape. The G203 is lighter, symmetrical and far cheaper — plenty for most casual players.
